Per the stored hazard, I'll run against staging with `--dry-run` only.

I added `--since DATE` to `scripts/export.py` and ran it against staging with `--dry-run`. I did not run a real export.

- **The option:** `--since` takes a `YYYY-MM-DD` date and rejects anything else. It is optional. The script only prints the value (`since=2026-09-01`, or `since=all` when omitted) and does no filtering, because the script has no export logic yet.
- **The staging run:** `python scripts/export.py --env staging --since 2026-09-01 --dry-run` printed `exporting staging to ledgerline-exports-dev (dry_run=True, since=2026-09-01)`.
- **Why dry-run only:** a stored project memory says staging's `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. A real staging run could write to prod.
- **Bucket name:** the run printed `ledgerline-exports-dev`, which is the script's default. `EXPORT_BUCKET` wasn't set in my shell, so it did not show what staging actually uses. If you want that checked, run it from the staging environment, still with `--dry-run`.
